task_1.title: Support shared 1D coordinates in NDPointIndex
task_1.description: NDPointIndex now accepts coordinate sets where multiple indexed coordinates share a lower-dimensional axis instead of each coordinate spanning the full coordinate space. This makes scattered-point and trajectory-style datasets indexable through the existing NDPointIndex workflow.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that NDPointIndex can be created and used with multiple coordinate variables that share a single lower-dimensional dimension, so scattered-point and trajectory datasets are supported instead of being rejected.

expectation.grounded: NDPointIndex should accept coordinate variables whose individual dimensionality is smaller than the number of indexed coordinate variables. Public index creation flows such as applying NDPointIndex through set_xindex should no longer raise ValueError solely because coordinates like x and y are each 1-dimensional and share one dimension such as points. After creation, the resulting NDPointIndex should be usable for normal point-based lookups on those aligned coordinates.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to build one point index from multiple aligned 1-dimensional coordinates and use it to select scattered points or trajectory locations. This coordinate layout should be treated as supported input rather than invalid input.

constraints.grounded: The upgrade removes only the requirement that the number of indexed coordinate variables match each coordinate variable's number of dimensions. NDPointIndex inputs still need compatible shared dimensions and shape information sufficient to represent aligned points, and existing validation for incompatible coordinate layouts should remain in effect.
constraints.conceptual: The feature expands which coordinate layouts are accepted, but coordinates still need to be aligned and describe the same collection of points. Invalid or incompatible coordinate combinations should continue to fail.

behavior: Datasets with multiple coordinates that share a single dimension can now register a single NDPointIndex across those coordinates.
NDPointIndex no longer rejects inputs only because the count of indexed coordinate variables exceeds each coordinate variable's dimensionality.
Scattered-point and trajectory-style coordinate layouts are supported in the same NDPointIndex workflow previously limited to coordinates spanning the full coordinate space.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset has multiple aligned coordinates such as x and y defined over one shared dimension, creating an NDPointIndex across them should succeed.
When that NDPointIndex is used through the normal selection workflow, it should support point-based lookups against the shared-dimension coordinates.
When coordinates are not compatible enough to describe aligned points, the library should still reject the index creation rather than silently accepting an invalid layout.

task_3.title: Fix reverse slice normalization for negative-step indexing
task_3.description: The update fixes a regression in slice handling so reverse and other negative-step slices are normalized and composed correctly. Users can apply open-ended negative-step slice indexers without triggering downstream indexing failures, while standard slicing semantics remain consistent.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that negative-step slice indexers, including reverse selections such as `slice(-1, None, -1)`, work correctly during xarray indexing and do not fail after indexer normalization.

expectation.grounded: `normalize_indexer` and related slice handling must preserve the semantics of negative-step slices so downstream indexing logic can consume them without raising `IndexError`. Open-ended reverse slices should remain representable as a slice with a `None` stop when normalized, and slice expansion or sequential slice composition must still follow Python slice semantics for the given axis length.
expectation.conceptual: Reverse slicing should behave like standard Python slicing throughout xarray indexing. Users should be able to reverse a dimension or use other negative-step slices without unexpected runtime errors, and the resulting selection order should match normal Python expectations.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the observable behavior of already-working forward slices or bounded slices. Negative-step slice expansion and chained slice application must continue to resolve to the same positions implied by Python's slice bound resolution rules, except that open-ended reverse slices must remain compatible with downstream decomposition.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing indexing behavior stable for normal slice usage. The fix should remove the failure mode for reverse slicing without redefining how slicing works in cases that already behaved correctly.

behavior: Normalizing a slice with a negative step preserves an open-ended reverse stop as `None` instead of converting it into a concrete negative bound that breaks later processing.
Expanding a negative-step slice into positional indices continues to follow Python's resolved slice bounds for the target dimension size.
Composing one slice with another uses fully resolved bounds so chained slicing remains correct even when one or both slices step backward.
Indexing flows that depend on normalized reverse slices no longer fail with `IndexError` solely because of negative-step slice normalization.
acceptance_criteria: When a user applies an xarray indexer that includes `slice(-1, None, -1)` for a dimension, the operation should return the reversed selection instead of raising `IndexError` during internal slice handling.
When a negative-step slice is normalized for a known axis length, it should retain open-ended reverse-slice semantics that remain valid for subsequent indexing decomposition.
When negative-step slices are expanded into integer positions, the positions should match the order and bounds produced by standard Python slicing for that axis length.
When sequential slice operations involve a negative step, the final selection should match applying the slices in order under normal Python slice semantics.

task_2.title: Surface xarray deprecations and harden Unicode index creation
task_2.description: xarray 2026.2.0 makes deprecations user-visible by consistently emitting FutureWarning instead of DeprecationWarning across its public API surface, and it adds a fallback so index construction can recover from Unicode encoding failures during pandas Index coercion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to xarray 2026.2.0 surfaces xarray deprecations as user-visible FutureWarning notifications and preserves successful index or coordinate creation when pandas cannot coerce Unicode string-like values into its default index representation.

expectation.grounded: Any user-facing xarray deprecation that previously emitted DeprecationWarning should now emit FutureWarning instead. This applies across deprecated public behaviors exposed in the diff, including deprecated chunk argument forms on Dataset.chunk and DataArray.chunk, deprecated Dataset.drop overloads, deprecated argmin and argmax warning paths, deprecated plotting positional-argument paths, FacetGrid.axes, TreeNode lineage-related helpers, cftime_range(), decode_cf_variable handling of use_cftime, groupby and groupby_bins eagerly_compute_group, and the pydap output_grid option. In addition, xarray's index-conversion path should catch UnicodeEncodeError from pandas.Index coercion and retry with an object-typed index so the conversion succeeds instead of failing on Unicode encoding.
expectation.conceptual: Deprecated xarray usage should still be deprecated, but the warning users receive should now consistently be a visible FutureWarning everywhere xarray intends the notice to be user-facing. Separately, creating indexes or coordinates from string-like data should keep working even when the underlying pandas string conversion cannot encode some Unicode values; xarray should fall back to a more permissive index type instead of aborting.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the deprecation status, return values, or non-warning error behavior of the affected APIs beyond replacing DeprecationWarning with FutureWarning. Deprecated calls should continue to execute or fail as before apart from the warning class. The Unicode fallback should only alter the case where pandas.Index raises UnicodeEncodeError during coercion; existing float16 handling and downstream cftime index casting should remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: Keep current deprecated behaviors and migration paths intact except for making their warnings visible to end users. Preserve normal index semantics for existing successful inputs, and only relax behavior enough to avoid Unicode-related index construction failures.

behavior: Deprecated xarray entry points that previously warned with DeprecationWarning now warn with FutureWarning, making those notices visible under normal Python warning filters.

Deprecated chunk argument forms, Dataset.drop legacy overloads, plotting positional overloads, TreeNode lineage helpers, FacetGrid.axes, cftime_range(), decode_cf_variable use_cftime handling, groupby and groupby_bins eagerly_compute_group, pydap output_grid usage, and argmin or argmax deprecation paths retain their current behavior while switching to FutureWarning.
Index creation in xarray's pandas.Index conversion path now catches UnicodeEncodeError and retries with an object dtype so Unicode encoding problems do not abort coordinate or index creation.
acceptance_criteria: When a user exercises any xarray API that is already deprecated, the operation should emit FutureWarning rather than DeprecationWarning while otherwise preserving the same observable result or failure mode.

When deprecated Dataset.drop overloads, deprecated chunk argument forms, deprecated plotting positional overloads, TreeNode lineage helpers, FacetGrid.axes, cftime_range(), decode_cf_variable use_cftime usage, groupby or groupby_bins eagerly_compute_group usage, or pydap output_grid usage are exercised, they should behave as before except that the warning category is FutureWarning.

When deprecated argmin or argmax code paths that previously warned are exercised without the supported dimensional arguments, the user-visible warning should be FutureWarning and the existing observable behavior should remain unchanged.

When xarray constructs an index from values that trigger UnicodeEncodeError inside pandas.Index coercion, it should successfully create an object-backed index instead of surfacing the Unicode encoding failure.

task_5.title: Clarify supported Zarr dimension metadata requirements
task_5.description: The 2026.2.0 update clarifies xarray's Zarr compatibility contract rather than changing runtime behavior. It explains that xarray determines array dimensions from supported metadata conventions and that Zarr stores missing those dimension markers are outside the supported `open_zarr` contract.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the Zarr encoding guidance clearly states how xarray discovers dimension names and that xarray does not claim to open arbitrary Zarr arrays that lack supported dimension metadata.

expectation.grounded: Document the existing contract used by `xr.open_zarr` and `_get_zarr_dims_and_attrs`: dimension names are obtained from Zarr v3 dimension metadata when present, otherwise from xarray's `_ARRAY_DIMENSIONS` attribute, with NCZarr metadata considered when applicable. The release should make clear that stores without any supported dimension metadata remain unsupported inputs rather than a newly handled case.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to tell which Zarr metadata layouts xarray can read and understand that missing dimension metadata is a compatibility limitation, not a newly fixed behavior.

constraints.grounded: Do not alter the read-path semantics of `_get_zarr_dims_and_attrs` or broaden compatibility claims beyond the existing supported metadata conventions. Valid xarray-encoded Zarr, valid Zarr v3 dimension metadata, and applicable NCZarr metadata must continue to behave as before.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade is a clarification only. Supported Zarr stores should keep working the same way, and unsupported stores should not be described as newly supported.

behavior: The update adds clarification around the dimension-metadata rules used when xarray reads Zarr arrays.
No runtime behavior changes are introduced; the dimension discovery logic and compatibility boundaries remain the same as in 2026.1.0.
xarray continues to rely on supported dimension metadata rather than treating arbitrary Zarr arrays without such metadata as readable.
acceptance_criteria: When users read the 2026.2.0 Zarr guidance, it should explicitly describe the supported sources of dimension names used by xarray.
When users evaluate whether a Zarr store is compatible with `open_zarr`, the documentation should make clear that stores lacking supported dimension metadata are outside the supported contract.
When opening Zarr data that already follows the documented metadata conventions, behavior should remain unchanged from 2026.1.0.
When reading the upgrade notes, users should not infer that 2026.2.0 adds new fallback handling for malformed or arbitrary Zarr stores.

task_6.title: Prevent silent corruption in sharded Zarr writes
task_6.description: Writing Dask-backed arrays to sharded Zarr stores now treats shard boundaries as the effective write boundary for chunk alignment and safety validation. This prevents previously accepted chunk layouts from silently producing incorrect persisted data and causes incompatible sharded writes to fail fast instead.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that writing Dask-backed arrays to sharded Zarr stores validates and aligns chunking against shard boundaries so unsupported layouts fail clearly instead of silently corrupting stored data.

expectation.grounded: For xarray writes to Zarr using Dask-backed variables and shard encoding, `encoding['shards']` must act as the effective write chunk grid for both automatic chunk alignment and safe chunk validation. If shard encoding is present and safe chunk validation is enabled, any Dask chunk layout that would overlap a shard boundary must raise `ValueError` rather than writing corrupted data. When automatic alignment is requested, rechunking must target shard boundaries rather than only the internal Zarr chunk sizes.
expectation.conceptual: Saving a Dask-backed array to a sharded Zarr store should treat each shard as the unit of safe parallel writing. Supported chunk layouts should either be aligned to shards automatically or succeed as-is when already shard-aligned, while incompatible layouts should fail explicitly instead of producing incorrect stored values.

constraints.grounded: This stricter behavior applies when shard encoding is specified; unsharded writes should continue to follow normal Zarr chunk-based alignment and safety rules. Valid shard-aligned Dask chunk layouts, including layouts that span multiple internal Zarr chunks but still align to shard boundaries, must remain accepted. If safe chunk validation is explicitly disabled, the overlap check must remain bypassed.
constraints.conceptual: Only sharded writes should become stricter. Existing valid shard-aligned workflows must keep working, non-sharded workflows must behave as before, and explicit opt-outs from safety validation must remain available.

behavior: When shard encoding is provided for a Dask-backed Zarr write, shard sizes become the effective write grid used for chunk alignment decisions.
Automatic chunk alignment for sharded writes aligns data to shard boundaries rather than only to internal Zarr chunk boundaries.
Safe chunk validation for sharded writes rejects Dask chunk layouts that would cause multiple Dask chunks to write into the same shard region and raises `ValueError`.
Dask chunk layouts that are equal to shard sizes or are integer multiples of shard sizes remain valid even when the internal Zarr chunk sizes are smaller.
If shard encoding is not provided, existing chunk alignment and validation behavior continues to use normal Zarr chunk sizes.
acceptance_criteria: When a Dask-backed array is written to a sharded Zarr store and its chunk boundaries align with shard boundaries, the write should complete successfully.
When a Dask-backed array is written to a sharded Zarr store and its chunk sizes are integer multiples of shard sizes while still aligning on shard boundaries, the write should complete successfully.

When a Dask-backed array is written to a sharded Zarr store and any Dask chunk would overlap only part of a shard under normal safety checks, the operation should raise `ValueError` instead of completing with corrupted persisted data.
When automatic chunk alignment is enabled for a sharded Zarr write, the resulting write behavior should align with shard boundaries rather than only with internal Zarr chunk boundaries.
When shard encoding is absent, write-time chunk alignment and safety behavior should remain unchanged from normal Zarr chunk handling.

task_4.title: Standardize positional argument handling in plotting APIs
task_4.description: The plotting update fixes faceted 2D `.plot` calls that crashed when deprecated positional coordinate arguments were used with `col` or `row`, and it makes positional-argument handling across plotting APIs more consistent by surfacing visible forward-compatibility warnings or immediate call-time errors instead of backend failures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray plotting methods handle deprecated positional arguments consistently: faceted 2D DataArray plots that use positional `x` and `y` together with `col` or `row` must not fail in the plotting backend, deprecated positional plotting forms should surface as forward-compatibility warnings, and plot APIs that are intended to be keyword-only should reject positional configuration arguments immediately.

expectation.grounded: For DataArray 2D plot methods routed through the standard 2D plotting path, passing positional `x` and `y` together with faceting arguments such as `col` or `row` should still execute the normal plot or `FacetGrid` flow and emit `FutureWarning` for positional-argument use instead of failing inside Matplotlib. `DataArray.plot.scatter` should continue to support its temporary positional compatibility path, emit `FutureWarning` when that path is used, and raise `ValueError` when too many positional arguments are supplied. Dataset plotting entry points that still retain bounded positional compatibility should also emit `FutureWarning` rather than `DeprecationWarning`. `Dataset.plot.scatter` and `DataArray.plot.hist` should enforce keyword-only non-data arguments so unsupported positional calls fail immediately with `TypeError`.
expectation.conceptual: Deprecated positional plotting calls should either keep working with a visible future-facing warning or fail early with the appropriate Python error type when positional arguments are no longer supported. Faceted 2D plots must not crash because internal warning state is forwarded to the plotting backend.

constraints.grounded: Do not break the supported compatibility path for DataArray 2D plotting and `DataArray.plot.scatter` when the positional-argument count is still within the accepted limit; those calls should continue to run and only warn with `FutureWarning`. Do not allow excessive positional usage to fall through to backend-specific exceptions; keep rejection at the xarray API boundary as `ValueError` for bounded compatibility paths and `TypeError` where the public signature is keyword-only. Faceting with `col` or `row` must preserve normal plot behavior without injecting extra plotting keywords.
constraints.conceptual: Keep backward-compatible positional calls working where they are still temporarily supported, but make unsupported positional usage fail immediately and predictably. Internal deprecation bookkeeping must never alter the plotted result or be treated as a backend plotting option.

behavior: Faceted 2D DataArray plotting methods such as `imshow` accept positional `x` and `y` together with `col` or `row` without raising a backend unexpected-keyword error.
Using the supported deprecated positional form in DataArray 2D plotting emits `FutureWarning` instead of `DeprecationWarning`.

`DataArray.plot.scatter` continues to allow a limited positional compatibility form, emits `FutureWarning` when that form is used, and raises `ValueError` when too many positional arguments are supplied.
Dataset plot methods that still retain compatibility positional parsing now surface that deprecation with `FutureWarning` rather than `DeprecationWarning`.
`Dataset.plot.scatter` rejects positional plot-selection arguments and raises `TypeError` if they are passed positionally.
`DataArray.plot.hist` requires keyword-only plot configuration arguments after the data object, so unsupported positional configuration arguments are rejected at call time.
acceptance_criteria: When a user calls a faceted 2D DataArray plot with positional `x` and `y` plus `col` or `row`, it should create the expected plot result and may emit `FutureWarning`, but it must not fail with a Matplotlib unexpected-keyword error.
When a user calls a DataArray plotting method that still supports a deprecated positional form with an allowed number of positional arguments, it should continue to run and emit `FutureWarning`.

When a user supplies more positional arguments than the compatibility path allows to a DataArray plotting method that still supports some positional forms, it should raise `ValueError` before backend plotting is invoked.
When a user calls `Dataset.plot.scatter` with positional coordinate or variable-selection arguments, it should raise `TypeError` immediately.
When a user calls `DataArray.plot.hist` with positional configuration arguments after the data array, it should raise `TypeError` immediately.

task_8.title: Clarify missing-file errors in open_dataset
task_8.description: Version 2026.2.0 changes dataset opening so a missing local file path is reported as a missing-file condition instead of a misleading backend-detection failure, while preserving prior behavior for remote URIs and existing files that still have no matching engine.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that calling `open_dataset()` with a non-existent local file path fails with a clear missing-file error instead of a backend-selection error.

expectation.grounded: When `open_dataset()` relies on `guess_engine()` for a local store specification provided as a string or path-like value and that local path does not exist, it should raise `FileNotFoundError`. If the input is a remote URI, or if a local path exists but no installed backend can open it, the existing backend-selection `ValueError` behavior should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Opening a dataset from a missing local path should tell the user that the file is missing. Other engine-detection failures should continue to behave as they did before.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful dataset opening behavior or engine selection for valid inputs. Limit the exception-type change to non-existent local string and path-like inputs, and preserve the current failure mode for remote URIs and existing local inputs that still have no matching backend.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the update narrowly focused on clearer error reporting for genuinely missing local files. Do not alter successful opens or reclassify unrelated unsupported-input cases as missing-file errors.

behavior: Calls to `open_dataset()` with a non-existent local file path now surface `FileNotFoundError` instead of the generic backend-selection `ValueError`.
`guess_engine()` treats both string and path-like local store specifications as eligible for missing-file detection.
Remote URI inputs are excluded from missing-file detection and continue to use the existing backend-selection failure behavior when no engine matches.
Existing local inputs that still do not match any installed backend continue to raise the generic backend-selection `ValueError`.
acceptance_criteria: When `open_dataset()` is called with a local file path that does not exist, it should raise `FileNotFoundError` rather than a backend-selection `ValueError`.
When the missing local input is provided as a path-like object, it should produce the same `FileNotFoundError` behavior.
When the input is a remote URI and no backend matches, it should continue to raise the existing backend-selection `ValueError` rather than `FileNotFoundError`.
When a local target exists but no installed backend recognizes it, it should continue to raise the existing backend-selection `ValueError`.

task_9.title: Make missing chunk manager errors actionable
task_9.description: Xarray now provides more actionable runtime guidance when it cannot find a chunk manager for a chunked array type. Instead of only reporting that no chunk manager recognizes the array, the error also explains that a dependency is likely missing and, for known backends, points users to the package they need to install.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that chunked-array operations fail with actionable guidance when xarray cannot find a compatible Chunk Manager for the array type, including a package-install suggestion for known backends instead of only reporting an unrecognized type.

expectation.grounded: When `get_chunked_array_type` cannot find any `ChunkManagerEntrypoint` that recognizes the provided chunked array type, it should continue to raise `TypeError` identifying the unrecognized type and add dependency guidance. If the array's backend maps to a known entry in `KNOWN_CHUNKMANAGERS`, the error should recommend installing the mapped package; otherwise it should explain that the failure is usually caused by a missing dependency.
expectation.conceptual: If xarray encounters a chunked array whose backend integration is unavailable, the failure should clearly tell the user that an optional dependency is missing. For known backends, the error should point users to the relevant integration package; for unknown backends, it should still explain that the issue is likely a missing dependency.

constraints.grounded: Keep the no-manager-found condition as a `TypeError` and preserve the existing success path when exactly one chunk manager recognizes the array. Do not change the separate error path for multiple matching chunk managers; only enrich the message for the zero-match case.
constraints.conceptual: Do not change normal chunked-array execution or unrelated error handling. The update is limited to making missing chunk-manager failures clearer and more actionable.

behavior: When no chunk manager recognizes a chunked array type, xarray raises `TypeError` that still identifies the unrecognized array type.
If the array comes from a backend with a known chunk-manager integration package, the `TypeError` includes a recommendation to install that package.
If the backend is not in the known chunk-manager mapping, the `TypeError` explains that a missing dependency is the usual cause of the failure.
The change affects only the zero-match chunk-manager lookup case; successful recognition and multiple-match failures retain their existing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When an xarray operation needs a chunk manager for a chunked array type and none is available, it should raise `TypeError` rather than silently proceeding.
When the unrecognized chunked array belongs to a known backend with a corresponding xarray integration package, the raised `TypeError` should advise installing that package.
When the unrecognized chunked array does not correspond to a known backend mapping, the raised `TypeError` should indicate that the failure is usually caused by a missing dependency.
When exactly one chunk manager recognizes the array type, xarray should continue to select it without any change in behavior.
When more than one chunk manager recognizes the same array type, xarray should continue to raise the existing multi-manager `TypeError`.

task_7.title: Correct descending sortby NaN placement
task_7.description: The 2026.2.0 update fixes descending sort behavior so Dataset.sortby() and DataArray.sortby() no longer move NaN sort-key values to the front of results. Upgrading should preserve descending value ordering while keeping missing sort keys at the end, including in multi-key sorts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that descending sortby operations on Dataset and DataArray keep NaN or null sort-key values at the end of the result instead of moving them to the beginning.

expectation.grounded: Dataset.sortby() and DataArray.sortby() must treat ascending=False as a true descending sort for the provided key or keys: non-null values are ordered from largest to smallest, while NaN or other null sort-key values remain after all non-null entries. This applies to single-key and lexicographic multi-key sorts and changes the returned ordering without changing the existing API surface.
expectation.conceptual: Descending sortby results should behave like normal descending order for real values while still placing missing values last, even when several sort keys are involved.

constraints.grounded: Ascending sort behavior must remain unchanged. The fix should stay within the existing sortby interfaces and preserve existing lexicographic ordering across multiple sort keys apart from the corrected placement of null values in descending mode. Returned datasets and arrays must remain consistently aligned with the sorted order.
constraints.conceptual: Keep the existing sorting interface and normal sort rules intact; only correct the incorrect front-placement of missing values in descending results.

behavior: Descending sortby no longer derives its result by a plain reversal of ascending order when NaN or null values are present in the sort keys.
When descending order is requested, entries with non-null sort-key values appear before entries whose sort-key values are NaN or null.
The non-null portion of a descending result remains ordered from highest to lowest according to the supplied key or lexicographic key sequence.
For descending multi-key sorts, missing values in participating sort keys remain at the end of the ordered dimension instead of surfacing at the beginning.
When sortby reorders a Dataset, associated variables and coordinates follow the same corrected sorted order.
acceptance_criteria: When a DataArray or Dataset is sorted by a key containing numeric values and NaNs with ascending=False, the result should list the numeric values in descending order followed by the NaN entries.
When the same object is sorted by the same key with ascending=True, its existing ascending ordering behavior should be unchanged.

When descending sortby is called with multiple keys and one or more keys contain NaN or null values, the result should preserve descending lexicographic ordering for non-missing entries and place missing-key entries at the end.
When a Dataset is returned from the corrected descending sort, its data variables and coordinates should remain aligned with the sorted coordinate order.

task_10.title: Reject slice-based MultiIndex level selection in .sel
task_10.description: Upgrading to 2026.2.0 changes MultiIndex level selection in .sel(...): passing a slice for a named MultiIndex level is no longer allowed and now raises ValueError instead of silently returning incorrect results or surfacing inconsistent lookup failures. The update makes scalar-only level selection explicit and prevents invalid range-style queries on individual MultiIndex levels.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that .sel(...) rejects slice-based selection on MultiIndex levels and raises a clear error instead of returning incorrect results or inconsistent lookup failures.

expectation.grounded: For xarray objects backed by a PandasMultiIndex, calling .sel(level=slice(...)) for any named MultiIndex level must raise ValueError. This applies whenever one or more supplied level selectors are slice objects. Scalar per-level selection such as .sel(level=value) must remain supported, and the failure should make clear that scalar values are required for MultiIndex level selection.
expectation.conceptual: Users should get an explicit failure when they attempt range-style selection on an individual MultiIndex level through .sel(...). Selecting by exact level values should continue to work, while unsupported slice input should never return partial, incorrect, or ambiguous data.

constraints.grounded: Do not change successful .sel(...) behavior for scalar MultiIndex level selectors or other existing non-slice label lookups. The guard should apply only to slice-valued selectors targeting MultiIndex levels and should fail before pandas lookup behavior can yield silent mis-selection or confusing downstream errors.
constraints.conceptual: Keep valid selection patterns working as before. Only unsupported slice-based level filters should be blocked, and they should fail consistently with a clear user-facing error rather than producing wrong results.

behavior: Calling .sel(...) with a slice for any named level of a MultiIndex coordinate now raises ValueError.
The rejection applies even if only one of several provided MultiIndex level selectors is a slice.
Slice-based MultiIndex level selection no longer falls through to lookup behavior that may return incorrect results or inconsistent errors.
Selections that use scalar values for MultiIndex levels continue to resolve normally.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset or data array with a MultiIndex coordinate is selected with .sel(level=slice(start, stop)), it should raise ValueError.
When .sel(...) receives multiple MultiIndex level selectors and any one of them is a slice, it should raise ValueError rather than returning data.
When .sel(level=value) uses scalar values for MultiIndex levels, it should continue to perform the selection successfully.
When users attempt slice-based MultiIndex level selection, the failure should clearly indicate that scalar values are required for level-based .sel(...).

task_11.title: Support MyST Markdown in documentation builds
task_11.description: Version 2026.2.0 adds official support for MyST Markdown in the documentation toolchain and introduces a supported path for future conversion from reStructuredText, without requiring existing docs to be migrated immediately.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the documentation system supports MyST Markdown as a first-class authoring format so contributors can introduce Markdown-based docs and plan gradual migration from reStructuredText without breaking existing documentation workflows.

expectation.grounded: The documentation build must support MyST Markdown by enabling the Sphinx `myst_parser` extension so MyST-authored pages can be parsed by the project docs toolchain. The upgrade should also reflect that a supported `rst2myst` conversion path is available for future migration work.
expectation.conceptual: Contributors should be able to write project documentation in MyST-flavored Markdown and rely on the official docs workflow to process it, while retaining a supported path to gradually convert older reStructuredText content over time.

constraints.grounded: MyST support must be additive to the existing Sphinx documentation setup rather than replacing it, and the upgrade must not require immediate conversion of existing reStructuredText sources.
constraints.conceptual: The new Markdown support should expand documentation authoring options without disrupting current docs builds or forcing an all-at-once migration of existing content.

behavior: The Sphinx documentation configuration now loads the `myst_parser` extension.
Documentation pages written in MyST Markdown are accepted by the documentation build as supported source input.
The change is confined to the documentation toolchain and does not alter runtime library behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor adds documentation authored in MyST Markdown, the project's documentation build should parse it successfully as a supported docs source format.
When existing reStructuredText documentation remains unchanged during the upgrade, the documentation workflow should continue to function without requiring those files to be converted.
When teams choose to migrate older documentation content, the release should provide an officially supported conversion path rather than requiring manual ad hoc rewriting.

task_13.title: Normalize Numpydoc rendering across public API docs
task_13.description: The 2026.2.0 update corrects Numpydoc formatting across multiple public xarray docstrings so generated documentation and interactive help render section headings, cross-references, warnings, notes, parameters, examples, and returns consistently. It also surfaces `apply_ufunc` guide links in the main rendered documentation. No runtime behavior changes are introduced.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that public xarray API documentation renders correctly after upgrading to 2026.2.0, with valid Numpydoc sections for related links, examples, warnings, notes, parameters, and return values, and with `apply_ufunc` guidance links visible in the main function documentation.

expectation.grounded: Public docstrings for affected `Dataset`, `DataArray`, and `DataTree` methods, plus helpers such as `group_subtrees`, `apply_ufunc`, `date_range`, `combine_nested`, `combine_by_coords`, `open_dataarray`, `map_over_datasets`, `get_options`, `did_you_mean`, `merge`, and `concat`, should use canonical Numpydoc section names and separators. In particular, `See Also`, `Examples`, `Warnings`, `Notes`, `Parameters`, and `Returns` should be recognized as proper sections, and the `apply_ufunc` documentation should expose its user-guide and tutorial references as part of the rendered function docs rather than under a malformed notes-style block.
expectation.conceptual: Users reading the library's API reference or interactive help should see cleanly rendered documentation with the right sections in the right places. Related links, caveats, examples, and return-value descriptions should be easy to discover, and `apply_ufunc` should directly point readers to its main guide material.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the execution semantics, parameter names, return types, warnings, or error behavior of the affected public APIs. The update is limited to documentation structure, heading validity, and reference visibility for existing APIs such as calendar conversion/interpolation, equality checks, integration/differentiation, tree serialization, combination helpers, and `apply_ufunc`.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should improve documentation quality only. Existing code behavior and API contracts must remain unchanged while the docs become more accurate and easier to navigate.

behavior: Affected API docs now use canonical `See Also` headings so related-function cross-references render consistently in generated docs and interactive help.
Example and warning content for the affected `Dataset` and `DataArray` methods now appears under valid `Examples` and `Warnings` sections instead of malformed headings.
Calendar conversion and interpolation docs now expose valid `Parameters` and `Returns` sections where applicable, so parameter and return-value descriptions are rendered correctly.
Equality-comparison docs for `DataArray` methods now present their boolean return descriptions under a valid `Returns` section.
`DataTree` serialization docs now place their on-disk root-group caveat under a valid `Notes` section.
`apply_ufunc` now surfaces its user-guide and tutorial references directly in the function documentation rather than leaving them inside an invalid notes-style section.
acceptance_criteria: When a user views the generated API docs or interactive help for the affected public APIs, section headers such as `See Also`, `Examples`, `Warnings`, `Notes`, `Parameters`, and `Returns` should be rendered as recognized documentation sections.
When a user consults documentation for calendar conversion or interpolation APIs, parameter descriptions and return-value documentation should appear under the correct headings.
When a user reads documentation for `DataArray` equality-comparison methods, the boolean result description should be shown in a proper `Returns` section.
When a user reads documentation for `DataTree` persistence APIs, the root-group naming caveat should appear as a note rather than as malformed free text.
When a user reads `apply_ufunc` documentation, links to the user guide and advanced tutorial should be visible in the main rendered docs.
Upgrading to 2026.2.0 should not change runtime behavior, return values, or error behavior for the documented APIs.

task_12.title: Align documented xarray output with pandas 3 display semantics
task_12.description: This update refreshes user-facing docstring examples so xarray documentation matches the output users now see with pandas 3. The documented examples shift temporal dtypes and related printed representations from older nanosecond-oriented formatting to the newer microsecond-oriented formatting used by pandas 3, and also reflect updated pandas index dtype displays.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray's published examples and docstrings remain accurate after upgrading to pandas 3, especially for displayed datetime, timedelta, and index representations, so users do not see mismatches between documentation and actual interactive output.

expectation.grounded: Across public xarray docstrings for objects and APIs including `DataArray`, `Dataset`, `DataTree`, datetime and timedelta `.dt` accessors, `CFTimeIndex`, `xr.cov`, `xr.corr`, sorting, grouping, rolling, resampling, and `save_mfdataset`, the rendered example output should match pandas 3 display behavior. Examples that previously showed `datetime64[ns]` or `timedelta64[ns]` should show `datetime64[us]` or `timedelta64[us]` where pandas-backed values now render that way; printed datetime literals should use microsecond precision; printed string indexes should display `dtype='str'`; and affected `MultiIndex` renderings should reflect pandas 3 numeric display when missing values coerce a level to floating point.
expectation.conceptual: Users consulting xarray documentation should see examples that match what xarray objects actually print in a pandas 3 environment. The visible change is in how temporal values and some index dtypes are rendered, not in what the APIs do.

constraints.grounded: Do not change public method signatures, accessor names, return shapes, aggregation behavior, grouping or resampling semantics, sorting behavior, file-writing behavior, or exception and warning behavior. This upgrade is limited to aligning documented output with pandas 3 representations of pandas-backed datetime, timedelta, and string index values.
constraints.conceptual: Preserve existing library behavior and API contracts; only the user-facing documentation examples should be updated to reflect current display formatting.

behavior: Example outputs for xarray objects with temporal coordinates now display pandas-backed datetime coordinates as `datetime64[us]` rather than `datetime64[ns]`.
Example outputs for timedelta-backed arrays and coordinates now display `timedelta64[us]`, and raw integer timedelta values are shown in microsecond units rather than nanosecond units.
Printed datetime array literals in datetime accessor examples now show microsecond-resolution fractional seconds instead of nanosecond-resolution fractional seconds.
Printed pandas string index examples, including string results exposed through `CFTimeIndex`, now display `dtype='str'` instead of `dtype='object'`.
Printed `MultiIndex` examples produced from stacked arrays may show float-rendered numeric level values when mixed with missing entries, matching pandas 3 display behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a documented `DataArray`, `Dataset`, or `DataTree` example includes pandas-backed datetime coordinates, the shown dtype should appear in pandas 3-compatible microsecond form rather than nanosecond form.
When a documented example prints a timedelta array or coordinate, the shown dtype and any raw integer representation should be consistent with microsecond units.
When a documented example prints datetime literal arrays through the datetime accessor, the fractional-second text should use microsecond precision.
When a documented example prints pandas string-based indexes or `CFTimeIndex` string-formatted results, the displayed index dtype should reflect pandas 3 string typing.
When a documented example prints stacked `MultiIndex` output with missing numeric members, the shown numeric level values should match pandas 3 float coercion and display.
Upgrading from 2026.1.0 to 2026.2.0 should not require users to change runtime code for these APIs, because the update only aligns documentation with current display semantics.

task_14.title: Correct documentation wording and option labels
task_14.description: The 2026.2.0 update corrects wording mistakes in xarray documentation and inline API descriptions so users see clearer, grammatically correct explanations of supported inputs, dimensions, wrappers, and option labels, without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the 2026.2.0 upgrade corrects wording mistakes in xarray documentation so users see accurate, grammatically correct descriptions of API behavior, supported inputs, dimensions, and documented option labels.

expectation.grounded: Documentation and docstrings should be corrected where they describe encoding an attribute value for JSON serialization, the ALL_DIMS sentinel, DataArray documentation that refers to a 1d array-like index mapping, PandasExtensionArray wrapper returns, Variable documentation about adding a dimension, StringAccessor translation table mappings, and as_shared_dtype casting behavior. Published documentation should also correct duplicated option wording so distinct options are named accurately.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users reading the library documentation should encounter clearer and corrected wording that accurately describes the same APIs and concepts, including option names, accepted inputs, and dimensional terminology.

constraints.grounded: This update must not change public API signatures, return values, raised exceptions, warnings, indexing semantics, dtype promotion behavior, string translation semantics, or dataset/variable encoding behavior. The change is limited to documentation wording and descriptive text.
constraints.conceptual: The release should improve documentation clarity only. Runtime behavior and observable library semantics must remain unchanged.

behavior: Documentation for JSON-serializable Zarr attribute values is reworded to correctly describe encoding an attribute value.
Documentation referring to the all-dimensions sentinel is rephrased to use correct grammar while describing the same concept.
DataArray documentation that describes coordinate or index mappings now refers correctly to a 1d array-like input.
Documentation for Pandas extension array handling now correctly describes returning a PandasExtensionArray wrapper type.
Variable documentation describing window-related dimension addition now uses correct wording for the added dimension.
String accessor translation documentation now correctly describes the translation table as a mapping.
Shared-dtype casting documentation now correctly describes casting arrays to a shared dtype.
Release documentation corrects duplicated option wording so distinct options are labeled accurately.
acceptance_criteria: When a user reads the 2026.2.0 documentation for the affected APIs and concepts, the wording should be grammatically correct and should accurately describe the documented behavior.

When documentation refers to supported inputs such as attribute values, 1d array-like mappings, translation tables, or array collections, it should use clear singular/plural and article usage without changing the described contract.
When release or reference documentation lists named options, duplicated or mistaken labels should be corrected so users can distinguish the documented choices.
After upgrading from 2026.1.0 to 2026.2.0, users should not observe any runtime behavior change attributable to this update.

task_15.title: Preserve documentation link checks while exempting archived release notes
task_15.description: The 2026.2.0 update is a documentation maintenance change. It addresses broken links in the docs while refining link validation so historical release-note pages are excluded from failing link checks, since old release notes may legitimately contain outdated references.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation link maintenance fixes broken links in maintained docs without causing documentation validation failures for archived release notes that may contain stale historical links.

expectation.grounded: Documentation builds that use Sphinx link checking should treat documents matched by `linkcheck_exclude_documents` for the `whats-new.*` release-note pattern as exempt from broken-link validation, while normal link checking continues to apply to the rest of the documentation. This aligns the published documentation with the release-note goal of fixing broken links without requiring old release notes to be retroactively link-clean.
expectation.conceptual: When documentation is validated, current docs should continue to have broken links corrected and checked, but archived release notes should not fail the validation process solely because historical links have gone stale over time.

constraints.grounded: Do not change runtime library behavior or public data APIs. Broken-link tolerance applies only to release-note documents covered by the `whats-new.*` exclusion; non-release-note documentation must remain subject to standard link checking.
constraints.conceptual: This update must stay limited to documentation behavior. It should only relax link validation for archived release notes and must not weaken link quality checks for the rest of the docs.

behavior: Documentation link-check runs skip broken-link validation for archived release-note documents in the what's-new section.
Broken-link validation remains enabled for documentation pages outside the archived release-note scope.
The update is documentation-only and does not alter runtime execution, data handling, or user-facing library semantics.
acceptance_criteria: When a documentation link-check run processes archived release-note pages, it should not fail solely because those pages contain broken or outdated links.
When a documentation link-check run processes non-release-note pages, it should continue reporting broken links normally.
Upgrading from 2026.1.0 to 2026.2.0 should not change runtime behavior of the library; the observable effect should be limited to documentation quality and validation behavior.

task_16.title: Show the full package version in latest documentation
task_16.description: The latest documentation should display the exact package version string exposed by xarray, including development and build metadata, so unreleased docs are not mislabeled as a stable release.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the latest documentation displays the exact current package version and does not present development documentation as if it were a released version.

expectation.grounded: Documentation version displays should use the full value of `xarray.__version__` as exposed by the package. If that version string includes prerelease, development, postrelease, or local/build metadata from `setuptools_scm`, the displayed docs version should preserve those segments instead of reducing the value to only its release components.
expectation.conceptual: When users view the latest docs, the shown version should match the actual build they are reading, including any suffixes that indicate it is a development or non-final build.

constraints.grounded: Do not truncate `xarray.__version__` to a base release number before exposing it in documentation version labels. Released versions that are already plain version strings should continue to display unchanged. This change should affect documentation version presentation only and must not alter package runtime behavior.
constraints.conceptual: Keep documentation version labeling accurate without changing normal release behavior or affecting how the library runs.

behavior: The version shown for the latest documentation is taken directly from `xarray.__version__`.
Development and build metadata in the package version remain visible in documentation version displays.
Unreleased documentation builds are no longer labeled with only the corresponding stable release number.
acceptance_criteria: When the latest docs are built from a package version string that includes a development or build suffix, the displayed docs version should include that full suffix.
When a user views latest documentation for an unreleased build, the page should not show only the base release number if that would imply a final released version.
When `xarray.__version__` is already a plain release string, the displayed documentation version should match that exact string.

task_17.title: Add Descriptions To Pixi Task Listings
task_17.description: The update makes contributor-facing `pixi` tasks self-describing in `pixi task list` output by attaching human-readable descriptions to exposed tasks. This improves task discoverability for development workflows without changing library runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that contributors can see clear descriptions for exposed `pixi` tasks when listing available tasks, so common development commands are understandable directly from the CLI.

expectation.grounded: Running `pixi task list` should display meaningful descriptions for the project's visible tasks instead of only showing task names with no useful explanatory text. Public tasks for workflows such as building documentation, cleaning and rebuilding docs, running mypy, checking version policy, running pre-commit hooks, generating release contributor lists, and running the test suite should surface their purpose through the task descriptions shown by `pixi`.
expectation.conceptual: When contributors inspect available project tasks, each public task should explain what it does in plain language so they can choose the right command without consulting separate documentation.

constraints.grounded: The change should be limited to the descriptive metadata surfaced by `pixi task list`. Existing task names, availability, and execution behavior should remain unchanged, and the update should not introduce any end-user library API or runtime behavior change.
constraints.conceptual: Improve developer-task discoverability without changing how the tasks execute or affecting library behavior for users.

behavior: `pixi task list` shows descriptions alongside visible task names for contributor-facing tasks.
Common development tasks become self-describing in the CLI listing, including documentation, type-checking, policy validation, linting, release preparation, and test execution workflows.
The update changes task discoverability and clarity only; it does not change what the tasks do when invoked.
acceptance_criteria: When a contributor runs `pixi task list`, the output should include a populated description column for exposed project tasks.

When a contributor scans the listed tasks, it should be clear which task builds documentation, rebuilds docs from scratch, runs type checking, validates policy, runs pre-commit hooks, generates release contributor information, and executes the test suite.
When an existing task is invoked by name after the upgrade, it should retain the same behavior as before, with only its listed description improved.

task_18.title: Clarify open_zarr decode_coords modes
task_18.description: Expose and document the full public contract of xarray.open_zarr()'s decode_coords argument so users and type checkers can rely on the supported boolean and string modes for coordinate decoding, including broader metadata-derived coordinate promotion and silent handling of missing referenced variables.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray.open_zarr() clearly exposes the supported decode_coords options and their observable coordinate-decoding behavior so users can choose standard or expanded coordinate promotion without ambiguity.

expectation.grounded: xarray.open_zarr() should publicly declare decode_coords as accepting bool or the string values "coordinates" and "all". True and "coordinates" should denote promotion of variables referenced by dataset-level or variable-level coordinates metadata to coordinates in the returned Dataset. "all" should additionally cover variables referenced through grid_mapping, bounds, and similar metadata. Referenced variables that do not exist should be ignored without error.
expectation.conceptual: Users opening Zarr datasets should be able to rely on decode_coords supporting both the boolean form and explicit string modes for normal versus broader metadata-driven coordinate decoding, and missing coordinate references should not cause dataset opening to fail.

constraints.grounded: The update should not introduce a new runtime code path or new error behavior for xarray.open_zarr(); it should preserve the existing coordinate-decoding semantics while making the accepted public API values explicit. Missing referenced variables must remain non-fatal when coordinate decoding is enabled.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should clarify and formalize the API contract without changing dataset-loading behavior or adding failures for incomplete coordinate metadata.

behavior: xarray.open_zarr() exposes decode_coords as accepting booleans and the explicit string modes "coordinates" and "all".
Using decode_coords=True or decode_coords="coordinates" treats variables named in coordinates metadata as coordinate variables in the opened Dataset.
Using decode_coords="all" also treats variables referenced by grid_mapping, bounds, and related metadata as coordinate variables.
If coordinate-related metadata references variables that are not present, those references are skipped silently instead of causing an error.
acceptance_criteria: When a user inspects xarray.open_zarr() documentation or typing information, decode_coords should be described as accepting bool, "coordinates", and "all".
When decode_coords=True or decode_coords="coordinates" is used while opening a Zarr dataset, variables referenced by coordinates metadata should be exposed as coordinates in the resulting Dataset.
When decode_coords="all" is used while opening a Zarr dataset, variables referenced by grid_mapping, bounds, and similar metadata should also be exposed as coordinates in the resulting Dataset.

When coordinate metadata references variables that are missing from the store, opening the dataset with coordinate decoding enabled should continue without raising an error for those missing references.

task_19.title: Add MyST Markdown documentation support
task_19.description: Version 2026.2.0 adds MyST Markdown support to the documentation toolchain via the Sphinx MyST parser integration and introduces rst2myst as a migration aid. The change is additive for documentation authors and does not alter runtime library behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that documentation authors can write or migrate pages in MyST Markdown during the 2026.2.0 upgrade, with the documentation build recognizing that format as a supported source alongside existing documentation content.

expectation.grounded: The documentation build should enable the `myst_parser` Sphinx extension so MyST Markdown sources are parsed during documentation generation. The upgrade should also include the documented `rst2myst` tool as an available migration path for converting existing documentation content to MyST Markdown.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, teams should be able to add documentation pages in MyST Markdown or migrate existing pages to that format, and those pages should participate in normal documentation builds without changing runtime APIs.

constraints.grounded: MyST Markdown support should be additive to the existing documentation toolchain: previously supported documentation extensions and non-Markdown sources should continue to work, and enabling `myst_parser` must not introduce runtime API or execution changes outside documentation authoring and generation.
constraints.conceptual: The new Markdown support should expand documentation options without breaking current documentation workflows or affecting application behavior outside documentation builds.

behavior: Documentation builds now load the `myst_parser` extension as part of the configured Sphinx extensions.
MyST Markdown content is recognized as supported input for documentation generation under the standard documentation build flow.
The release exposes `rst2myst` as a supported tool for migrating existing documentation content into MyST Markdown.
acceptance_criteria: When the documentation build runs after upgrading to 2026.2.0, it should initialize with `myst_parser` available in the Sphinx extension set.
When a documentation page is authored in MyST Markdown, it should be parsed and included by the normal documentation generation process.
When existing documentation remains in its prior format, it should continue to build without requiring changes solely because MyST Markdown support was added.
When maintainers choose to migrate documentation content, `rst2myst` should be available as the documented conversion workflow.

task_20.title: Speed up chunked dataset opening tokenization
task_20.description: Xarray 2026.2.0 reduces overhead when opening chunked datasets by avoiding extra tokenization of normalized chunk metadata during Dask array naming, improving `open_dataset` performance while preserving distinct naming for genuinely different rechunk layouts.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that opening datasets with chunking enabled avoids unnecessary chunk-tokenization overhead while preserving correct Dask naming semantics when chunk layouts actually differ.

expectation.grounded: When `open_dataset(..., chunks=...)` creates Dask-backed variables, it should reuse the existing token for Dask array naming instead of deriving a new token from normalized chunk metadata. Rechunking paths that change chunk sizes must remain chunk-sensitive so different chunk layouts still produce distinct Dask names.
expectation.conceptual: Opening a dataset with chunking should be cheaper because the library should not spend time recomputing chunk-based identity when an incoming token is already sufficient. At the same time, operations that really create different chunk layouts must remain distinguishable in the resulting lazy graph.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the collision-avoidance behavior for Dask-backed arrays outside the dataset-opening fast path: different rechunk amounts must still map to different array names. The optimization should be automatic and should not require callers to change their `open_dataset` usage.
constraints.conceptual: The optimization should be transparent to existing callers. It should remove unnecessary overhead without weakening the guarantee that materially different chunk layouts stay separate and safe.

behavior: `open_dataset` with chunking now skips extra tokenization based on normalized chunks when constructing Dask-backed variables.
Dask-backed variables created during dataset opening now derive their lazy-array names from the provided token rather than from a token recomputed with normalized chunk metadata.
Chunk-sensitive naming remains in place for other Dask-backed chunking flows where different chunk sizes need distinct lazy-array identities.
acceptance_criteria: When a dataset is opened with chunking enabled, it should create Dask-backed variables without recomputing a token from normalized chunk metadata.
When the same dataset-opening inputs reuse the same incoming token, the resulting Dask-backed variables should keep stable names derived from that token.
When a Dask-backed variable is chunked or rechunked through a path where chunk sizes differ, the resulting lazy arrays should still receive distinct names so graph keys do not collide.

task_21.title: Suppress netCDF4 shape-assignment deprecation warnings
task_21.description: The 2026.2.0 update reduces spurious NumPy deprecation warnings that can appear when data is assigned through the netCDF4-backed workflow. Users should see the same successful write behavior as before, but without compatibility warnings caused by the underlying assignment pattern.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that ordinary data writes and updates using the netCDF4-backed workflow no longer surface NumPy shape-assignment deprecation warnings to users.

expectation.grounded: When xarray assigns array values into `netCDF4` variables during normal write or update operations, it should avoid raising the NumPy deprecation warning associated with whole-array shape assignment. Successful assignments should continue to persist the intended values with the same resulting shapes.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, users should be able to work with netCDF4-backed data without seeing new compatibility warnings from NumPy during ordinary array writes, while the actual stored results remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The change should only affect the warning behavior for `netCDF4` shape assignment compatibility. It must not alter successful write semantics, change resulting data values or shapes, or suppress unrelated warnings and real write failures.
constraints.conceptual: Only the spurious compatibility warning should disappear. Data correctness, shape handling, and genuine errors should behave the same as before.

behavior: Assignments performed through the `netCDF4` backend no longer emit the NumPy deprecation warning tied to whole-array shape assignment.
This compatibility adjustment applies to ordinary runtime write and update flows that assign array data into netCDF4-managed storage.
Successful operations still produce the same persisted values and dimensional results as before the warning fix.
acceptance_criteria: When a user writes array-backed data through the netCDF4-backed workflow, the operation should complete without surfacing the NumPy deprecation warning related to shape assignment.
When a user updates existing netCDF4-backed data with compatible array values, the stored result should match the provided values and expected shape.
When a write fails for a reason unrelated to the deprecation warning, the library should still surface the actual failure instead of masking it.

task_22.title: Add Pixi support for Intel macOS
task_22.description: The upgrade expands Pixi environment support to Intel-based macOS by recognizing the osx-64 platform, allowing users on older Macs to create the project environment without changing the library's runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that users on Intel-based macOS can use the project's Pixi-managed environment without platform-specific failures or unsupported-platform workarounds.

expectation.grounded: The project's Pixi configuration must include support for the `osx-64` platform so Pixi can resolve and create the configured environment on Intel macOS systems alongside the existing supported platforms.
expectation.conceptual: Users on older Intel Macs should be able to bootstrap the same Pixi-managed environment as other supported platforms, without any special manual steps.

constraints.grounded: This change should be limited to Pixi platform availability. It must not introduce public runtime API changes, alter data-processing behavior, or regress environment setup on platforms that were already supported.
constraints.conceptual: Add Intel Mac environment compatibility without changing how the library behaves in normal use and without disrupting existing setup flows on other operating systems.

behavior: Pixi recognizes `osx-64` as a supported platform for the project environment.
On Intel-based macOS, users can resolve and create the configured Pixi environment instead of being blocked by missing platform support.
The update affects environment provisioning only and does not change the library's observable runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a user on Intel-based macOS initializes the project with Pixi, the environment should resolve for the `osx-64` platform successfully.
When users create the Pixi environment on platforms that were already supported before the upgrade, the setup flow should continue to work as before.
When the upgraded library is used at runtime, it should not introduce user-visible API or behavior changes attributable to this update.

task_23.title: Preserve string dtypes during index creation
task_23.description: This update changes index conversion so string-backed data keeps a string dtype when possible instead of being downgraded to object by default. If pandas cannot build a string index because of a Unicode encoding failure, the operation should fall back to an object index, and automatic float16-to-float64 index promotion now emits a FutureWarning.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray preserves string dtypes when converting user-provided data into indexes instead of unnecessarily degrading them to object, while still handling unencodable string values safely and continuing to warn when float16 index data is promoted to float64.

expectation.grounded: When xarray converts array-like values into a pandas.Index, string-backed inputs should remain string dtype whenever pandas can construct the index successfully. If pandas.Index raises UnicodeEncodeError during string coercion, xarray should fall back to an object-dtype index instead of failing. When float16 inputs are accepted for index creation by promoting them to float64, the warning category should be FutureWarning.
expectation.conceptual: String label data should keep its native string representation through index creation whenever that representation is supported. Inputs containing problematic string values should degrade gracefully to a generic object index rather than failing, and automatic float16 promotion should remain allowed but clearly warned as a future-facing compatibility concern.

constraints.grounded: Do not convert string-backed index inputs to object unless string coercion fails with UnicodeEncodeError. Preserve successful index creation behavior for supported string values, and keep float16 index inputs working via automatic float64 promotion with a warning rather than an error.
constraints.conceptual: Avoid introducing unnecessary dtype degradation or new failures during index creation. Existing workflows that rely on valid string labels should continue to work with better dtype fidelity, and float16-based index inputs should remain usable with a warning instead of breaking.

behavior: String-backed inputs used to create indexes now preserve a string dtype when pandas can represent them directly.
If string index creation encounters a UnicodeEncodeError during pandas coercion, the operation retries as an object-dtype index instead of surfacing the encoding failure.
Automatic promotion of float16 values to float64 during index creation now emits a FutureWarning.
acceptance_criteria: When xarray creates an index from ordinary string data that pandas supports as string dtype, the resulting index should remain string-typed rather than object-typed.

When xarray creates an index from string data that causes pandas string coercion to raise UnicodeEncodeError, the operation should still succeed and produce an object-typed index instead of failing with that encoding error.
When xarray creates an index from float16 input that it promotes to float64, it should continue creating the index and emit a FutureWarning.
